title: Load-bearing engineered living materials for ordinary structures

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a structural material made through biological activity that can carry ordinary building loads while retaining useful living functions during service. Organisms would help produce a solid component of a specified shape, and living cells within the material would subsequently help detect damage, reinforce damaged regions or restore mechanical capacity. The target combines structural performance, biological manufacture and living maintenance in the same component.

The intended application is building-scale elements produced on a construction timetable—proposed here as weeks or months—and durable enough for their stated service conditions. Biological fabrication alone would not establish the full concept: a component whose organisms cease functioning after manufacture would demonstrate a different capability. Likewise, placing a biological coating on a conventional load-bearing scaffold would not by itself demonstrate a living structural solid.

significance.text: If achieved, this combination would make biological activity part of both structural manufacture and subsequent maintenance. A component could potentially respond locally to damage through its own living constituents, rather than relying entirely on externally applied repairs. That would add a useful structural capability, but extending service life would require evidence that repair remains effective under repeated damage and realistic exposure conditions.

Timber shows that biological production can create strong structural material, but conventional load-carrying wood does not retain living cells responsible for maintaining its load-bearing tissue. Harvesting is not what creates that distinction. The more relevant biological analogy for the proposed maintenance function is a rigid material that remains populated and maintained by living cells, as discussed through bone in the supplied perspective. That analogy identifies a functional goal; it does not establish that building components can reproduce bone's behavior.

Achieving wood-like properties would not make the material a section-for-section replacement for steel. Heveran and Hernandez illustrate the stiffness difference with a comparison involving roughly 30 times the column area or beam flexural rigidity to obtain similar deflection behavior. This is a particular structural comparison, not a universal multiplier for every member dimension. Useful living structural materials could therefore require different member sizes, geometries and structural systems.

Conditional synthesis: reliable living repair could reduce some repair interventions, and economical biological fabrication could create additional manufacturing options. Lower cost, lower environmental impact and longer service life would each need separate demonstration. They do not follow automatically from biological production, a high strength measurement or one successful repair.

missing_breakthrough.text: The capability sought is the simultaneous achievement of adequate stiffness, strength, durability and sustained useful cellular activity in a structural solid. In their 2023 perspective, Heveran and Hernandez reported that engineered living materials with Young's modulus above 1 GPa sufficient to replace some common load-carrying materials had not been demonstrated. This is a documented historical gap; the supplied evidence does not establish whether the combined target remains unmet on 1 November 2026.

Stiffness and strength solve different engineering problems. Young's modulus describes resistance to elastic deformation, whereas compressive or flexural strength concerns failure under the corresponding loading. A material can resist substantial compressive stress yet deform too much for a particular structural use. Raising strength therefore does not, by itself, resolve the stiffness gap, and neither property alone establishes the suitability of a building element.

The living function must also survive the conditions associated with structural service. The perspective identifies prolonged cellular viability and extension of service life as central challenges, alongside rigidity and durability. Producing a rigid solid through cellular activity is distinct from keeping that solid populated by cells capable of useful maintenance. Damage detection or local reinforcement must ultimately translate into measurable recovery of structural performance.

Proposed engineering requirements: manufacture must scale from specimens to useful member dimensions while delivering consistent properties, acceptable production time and manageable repair conditions. Weeks-to-months fabrication is an additional requirement selected for this concept, not a demonstrated biological speed limit. Practical development would need to establish whether production and maintenance conditions can be accommodated in an ordinary building.

current_state.text: The supplied research identifies the principal source as Heveran and Hernandez's Matter perspective, “Make engineered living materials carry their weight,” dated 1 November 2023. The supplied review verified the accepted manuscript's identity and assessed its full text; the source index records an untruncated extraction without reported extraction issues. The title page did not independently establish the supplied publication date. The research reported that the publisher's full text did not load, but the accepted manuscript provides the basis for the supported historical findings.

That perspective summarized then-demonstrated stiff engineered living materials with Young's modulus reaching approximately 300 MPa, often below 10 MPa, and compressive strength around 1–5 MPa. It connected these properties with low-load applications such as paving tiles. Its comparison table gives pine a Young's modulus of 7.38 GPa and concrete approximately 30 GPa, with concrete compressive strength of 20–30 MPa. These are comparison values reported by the source, not universal specifications for all pine or concrete.

The perspective suggests that increasing compressive strength toward concrete-like values, for example above 20 MPa, would open additional building and infrastructure applications. This is a statement about prospective application breadth. It is not evidence that a living material had reached that performance, nor does it make 20 MPa a sufficient acceptance criterion for every structural use.

The supplied research separately lists “Engineered living building material for low-energy construction on Mars,” attributed to a ScienceDirect record dated 10 September 2026. It describes an abstract-level extract reporting mean compressive and flexural strengths of approximately 12 and 6 MPa, respectively, a hybrid gelatin and engineered-yeast binder, and a stated need for stronger, fully biological binders. These remain unverified descriptions from the research input: no source text was saved for the supplied review, and neither full text nor an author list was available in the research record. The review therefore could not assess the article's identity, measurements, composition or claimed practical limitations. This evidence limitation does not establish that the reported results are false.

Even if the later report's stated strength values are accurate, compressive and flexural strengths alone cannot determine Young's modulus. The supplied evidence consequently establishes neither that this material clears the 1 GPa stiffness benchmark nor that it fails it. With no supplied freshness search record and no captured text for the later source, the evidence supports the 2023 historical assessment but cannot establish the field's overall position on 1 November 2026.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: produce structural elements sized for a one- or two-storey building through a living process in weeks or months, and demonstrate compliance with a recognized code's applicable gravity-load strength and serviceability requirements. Report element geometry, loading, production time and the environmental conditions required during fabrication. A paving tile or laboratory cube would provide useful material evidence but would not satisfy this building-scale demonstration.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: As additional proposed material benchmarks, target a measured Young's modulus on the order of the perspective's pine value, approximately 7 GPa, or compressive strength above 20 MPa. These reference points have a source basis, but their use here is a proposal. Passing either benchmark must be accompanied by element-level verification of both adequate strength and stiffness; neither alternative is a substitute for structural design or an established consensus threshold.
completion_criteria.label: As additional proposed material benchmarks, target a measured

completion_criteria.text: Proposed repair demonstration: damage a structural element, measure its loss of capacity, permit repair under explicitly stated conditions and measure the fraction of capacity recovered. Include controls sufficient to distinguish the contribution of living activity from passive material changes. Report cellular viability and any required moisture, nutrients or other maintenance inputs. One event would establish a repair capability under those conditions; repeated events and a stated durability test period would be needed to support broader maintenance claims.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed repair demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundary checks: repeat manufacture and repair across independently produced batches and, where feasible, independent testing teams. Report variability, failures, relevant service exposures and cost against timber or concrete providing the same structural function. State which loads, environments, member dimensions and test durations were demonstrated. Finite testing can establish that breadth of performance without proving suitability for every building or indefinite service.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundary checks

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: CIV-04, “Repeated recovery of structural load capacity after cracking,” has the closest functional overlap. CIV-07 requires a useful living structural material, whereas CIV-04 focuses on repeated recovery of capacity regardless of repair mechanism. One living repair event would not establish CIV-04's repeated-recovery objective. CIV-03, “In-place conversion of ordinary ground into a specified engineering solid,” could share biological solidification methods, but its defining objective is ground conversion in place; CIV-07 concerns living load-bearing materials and their continuing function.

Roster-based synthesis: CIV-01, “A primary structural binder at global cement scale without process carbon dioxide,” concerns binder production, emissions and scale. A living binder might overlap, but CIV-07 does not inherently establish those outcomes. CIV-05, “Tensile-ductile mineral structures that replace reinforced concrete at ordinary cost,” concerns tensile ductility and economical structural substitution; a living material need not be mineral, tensile-ductile or cost-competitive. CIV-11, “Default-cost reinforcement with carbon-steel behavior and no corrosion in ordinary exposures,” addresses reinforcement performance and corrosion rather than living structural maintenance.

Roster-based synthesis: CIV-12, “Fail-safe adaptive primary structural response at ordinary-building cost,” overlaps with the broader idea of responsive structures, but living repair does not by itself establish fail-safe adaptation or ordinary-building cost. CIV-09, “Immediate building occupancy after the design earthquake, at life-safety cost,” is a whole-building seismic outcome; biological repair after damage does not establish immediate occupancy. CIV-10, “Structural concrete that stores building-relevant energy,” shares multifunctional structural design, but energy storage and living maintenance are distinct capabilities.

Roster-based synthesis: CIV-02, “Mechanics-based prediction of earthquake liquefaction and its ground consequences,” addresses predictive geomechanics; CIV-06, “Underground routes and spaces at surface-infrastructure cost,” addresses underground construction economics; and CIV-08, “Large-reservoir storage that passes sediment without giving up carryover water,” addresses reservoir operation and sediment transport. Living structural materials could eventually serve some associated infrastructure, but achieving CIV-07 would not establish any of these separate capabilities.

change_log.change: Recast the claimed missing material as a proposed combined capability and dated the documented stiffness gap to the 2023 perspective.
change_log.reason: The supplied evidence establishes a historical finding but lacks the freshness record needed to establish present-day absence.

change_log.change: Integrated sustained cellular viability, durability and living maintenance into the concept and technical barriers.
change_log.reason: The review identifies these as central challenges that are not captured by strength and stiffness alone.

change_log.change: Corrected the timber comparison and distinguished biological fabrication from sustained living function.
change_log.reason: Conventional load-carrying wood lacks living maintenance cells before harvest; harvesting is not the cause of that distinction.

change_log.change: Preserved the supported historical property ranges and specified the table's pine modulus as 7.38 GPa.
change_log.reason: The reviewed manuscript supports these quantitative comparisons, with the limitation that they are reference values rather than universal specifications.

change_log.change: Retained the 2026 report's numerical and compositional descriptions with explicit attribution and access limitations.
change_log.reason: They preserve potentially useful research detail without presenting an uncaptured abstract-level description as verified evidence.

change_log.change: Removed the conclusion that the 2026 material fails the 1 GPa stiffness benchmark.
change_log.reason: The later source was unavailable for review, and compressive and flexural strengths cannot by themselves establish Young's modulus.

change_log.change: Clarified the steel comparison as a source-specific distinction between column area and beam flexural rigidity.
change_log.reason: The reported comparison does not prescribe one universal member-size multiplier.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed demonstration to require element-level strength and serviceability, quantified living repair, viability, durability, reproducibility and functional cost comparison.
change_log.reason: A material benchmark or single repair event alone would not demonstrate the intended building-scale capability.

change_log.change: Added distinctions across the supplied concept roster and qualified downstream benefits.
change_log.reason: Shared applications or mechanisms do not merge the entries, and biological manufacture does not automatically establish cost, environmental or service-life advantages.

unresolved_issues: Whether any demonstration available by 1 November 2026 achieves the combined target remains unresolved because the supplied freshness record is empty.
The 2026 Martian building-material report's identity, publication date, author list, specimen scope, numerical results, binder composition and practical limitations require assessable source text.
No inspected evidence establishes the 2026 material's Young's modulus or whether it retains useful living functions under structural service conditions.
The 2023 publication date is supplied by the research metadata but was not independently established by the reviewed manuscript's title page.
Acceptable recovery fraction, number of repair cycles, durability duration and allowable maintenance inputs remain to be specified for a concrete demonstration.
The weeks-to-months production target, reproducible building-scale manufacture and competitive cost remain proposed requirements without demonstrated feasibility in this record.

The review's recommendation to omit the unavailable 2026 report's numerical and compositional details entirely was not adopted. Those details are retained solely as explicitly unverified research descriptions to preserve useful information without treating it as established evidence.
